## The gap narrowed between 1950 and 2019

Europe's life expectancy estimate exceeded Africa's by 21.8 years in 1950 and by 13.6 years in 2019. It reached 23.0 years in 1960 and 1961, narrowed to 16.6 in 1994 and 1995, then widened to 18.1 in 2001 before falling to 13.6 in 2019. The gap is calculated as Europe's estimate minus Africa's in each year; it is not a difference between individuals.

```chart
type: line
title: The Europe–Africa life expectancy gap narrowed
subtitle: Europe minus Africa, 1950–2019
data: {csv: data.csv}
encoding: {x: year, y: gap}
axes:
  x: {label: Year, format: year}
  y: {label: Difference, unit: ' years'}
style: {points: all, curve: linear}
```

*Source: Gapminder, life expectancy at birth, version 15 (5 April 2026), regional averages weighted by population; [gapminder.org](https://www.gapminder.org/data/), CC BY 4.0. The gap is calculated by subtraction.*
